title: docs(deployment): correct Turso/libSQL backup guidance in backup-restore.mdx
body:
Fixes #20430

Corrects a false statement in `content/docs/deployment/backup-restore.mdx` (was at `:74` on `origin/main` `e4d3f2ca6`). The "Managed databases" section said "(Turso/libSQL applies only to ObjectStack Cloud-managed environments — the open framework does not ship that driver.)" `@objectstack/driver-turso` is a published, optional driver (`packages/drivers/driver-turso/package.json` `publishConfig.access: public`) and is documented in `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx` and `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`.

## Before

```
### Managed databases (hosted Postgres, MongoDB Atlas, …)

Use the provider's snapshot, branching, or point-in-time-restore facilities.
Nothing ObjectStack-specific applies. (Turso/libSQL applies only to ObjectStack
Cloud-managed environments — the open framework does not ship that driver.)
```

## After

```
### Managed databases (hosted Postgres, MongoDB Atlas, …)

Use the provider's snapshot, branching, or point-in-time-restore facilities.
Nothing ObjectStack-specific applies.

**Turso / libSQL** (`@objectstack/driver-turso`) is a published, optional
driver in the open framework — see
[Turso / libSQL needs one extra install](/docs/data-modeling/drivers#url--driver-inference-table).
Its backup path depends on which of its three
[modes](/docs/plugins/packages#objectstackdriver-turso) a datasource runs in:

- **`local`** — a plain SQLite file (or `:memory:`) via the same
  Knex + `better-sqlite3` engine as the [SQLite section](#sqlite-single-host)
  above. Back it up the same way.
- **`replica`** — an embedded replica: a local SQLite file kept in sync from a
  remote database. The durable state is that local file, so the SQLite backup
  procedure above applies to it too; the remote side is the provider's.
- **`remote`** — pure `@libsql/client` requests over HTTP/WebSocket, with no
  local file. There is nothing on this host to back up; use the snapshot or
  point-in-time-restore facilities of whatever runs the remote libSQL server
  (Turso's managed service, or a self-hosted `sqld`), the same as any other
  managed database above.
```

## What was measured (file:line on `origin/main` `e4d3f2ca6`)

- `packages/drivers/driver-turso/package.json:` `publishConfig.access: public` — the driver is a real, published npm package, not Cloud-only.
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx:194,199` — the `### @objectstack/driver-turso` heading and "**Modes**: `local` (file / `:memory:` via better-sqlite3), `replica` (local file synced from a remote database), `remote` (pure `@libsql/client` over HTTP/WebSocket — no native bindings, so it runs on serverless/edge)". Measured, not copied from the card's "local, embedded-replica and remote" wording — the driver's own JSDoc (`packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts:7-9`) and this table both spell the mode `replica`, not "embedded-replica".
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx:49,55-69,81` — the URL-inference table and the "Turso / libSQL needs one extra install" callout: `libsql://` / `*.turso.io` URLs are inferred by the CLI and standalone runtime alike; `@objectstack/driver-turso` is an optional peer install (not shipped by default, but shipped as a first-party package — distinct from "not shipped").
- No page documents a distinct backup *procedure* for `replica` or `remote` mode beyond what the mode itself implies (a local SQLite file for `local`/`replica`, no local file for `remote`), so I did not invent one — I named what the driver's own code makes true for each mode and pointed to the existing SQLite backup steps and to the existing "Managed databases" pattern (provider snapshot) for `remote`, rather than writing a new procedure.

**PM review fix:** the "modes" link originally pointed at `drivers.mdx#supported-drivers`, which has no mode text. The three modes are documented at `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx:199` under the `### @objectstack/driver-turso` heading (`:194`). Re-pointed the link there, using the `github-slugger`-derived fragment `#objectstackdriver-turso` (verified: `slugger.slug('@objectstack/driver-turso') === 'objectstackdriver-turso'`), and confirmed with `check:doc-anchors` (`✅ check-doc-anchors: 387 internal #fragment link(s) across 412 source file(s) all resolve to a real heading`).

## Scope

`content/docs/deployment/backup-restore.mdx`, "Managed databases" section only, as claimed. No changeset (docs-only, not part of any package's published `files[]`).
